How to ask customers for Google reviews

Most happy customers never leave a review unless someone asks. Asking is allowed and expected. The way you ask decides whether the reviews stay up, so this page covers the ask, the link, the timing and the three mistakes that get reviews removed.

Write your requests free, in your browser

The three mistakes

  1. Offering something for the review. A discount, a free item or an entry into a draw, in return for a review, is against Google's policy. Say thank you instead.
  2. Review gating. Asking everyone how they felt and only sending the happy ones to the public page is selectively soliciting positive reviews, which Google prohibits. Send every customer the same request.
  3. Asking for a rating. “Please leave us five stars” turns feedback into a favour. Ask for honest feedback, good or bad.

Make it one tap

Every extra step costs responses. Use your direct review link, so the customer lands on the review box, not your listing. Review Reply Desk builds the link from your Google Place ID or accepts the g.page link from your Business Profile.

When to ask

Within a day or two of the visit or job, at a calm moment: after the invoice is paid or the work is signed off, not mid-job. Add a line to receipts and invoices so customers who skip the message still have the link.

Scripts that follow the rules

These are written by Review Reply Desk and the test suite recomputes them and runs them through the same checker, so they match what the tool writes today.

Text message

Hi Maria, thanks for choosing Luigi's Trattoria. Would you share your honest feedback? It takes a minute and helps others decide: https://g.page/r/your-business/review Reply STOP to opt out.

Email

Subject: Your honest feedback on Luigi's Trattoria

Hi Maria,

Thanks for choosing Luigi's Trattoria. Whatever your experience was, a short honest review helps us improve and helps other people decide.

https://g.page/r/your-business/review

It takes about a minute. If something went wrong, the review is the place to say so and we will read it.

Thank you,
Luigi

Receipt or counter card

How was your visit? Tell us honestly, good or bad: https://g.page/r/your-business/review

Texting customers

Only text people who gave you their number and agreed to hear from you, and always include a way to opt out. The rules differ by country and state; this page is general information, not legal advice.

Questions

Is it allowed to ask customers for Google reviews?

Yes. Google encourages businesses to ask customers to leave reviews and lets you share a direct link to your review form. What is not allowed is offering something in return, asking only the customers you expect to be happy, or discouraging negative reviews.

What is review gating?

Review gating means screening customers first, for example asking how their experience was and only sending the happy ones to the public review page. Google's policy prohibits selectively soliciting positive reviews, so send the same request to every customer.

Can I give a discount for a review?

No. Offering a discount, gift or entry into a draw in exchange for a review breaks Google's policy, and rules on bought reviews, such as the FTC's, point the same way. Say thank you instead. This is not legal advice.

When is the best time to ask for a review?

Soon after the job or visit, while it is fresh, and at a moment the customer is not rushed: after the invoice is paid or the work is signed off. A text or email within a day or two works better than a request weeks later.

How do I get my Google review link?

Open your Business Profile on Google, choose Ask for reviews, and copy the link, or use your Place ID with Google's write-review format. Paste either into Review Reply Desk and it builds the link for you.

Do I need permission to text customers?

Texting people without their agreement can break telephone and carrier rules in many places. Only text customers who gave you their number and agreed to be contacted, and include a way to opt out. Ask your own adviser what applies to you.

How to respond to a negative Google review

A bad review is read by far more people than the one who wrote it. Prospective customers skim the star rating, then read how the owner answered the worst one. A calm, short, specific reply is the cheapest marketing a local business has; an angry one is the most expensive.

Write your replies free, in your browser

The five rules

  1. Thank them and use their first name. Not their full name, and never their order or visit details.
  2. Apologise for the experience, not for legal fault. “We are sorry this was not the experience we want anyone to have” admits nothing. Skip “sorry if you feel…”, which reads as a non-apology.
  3. Name one specific thing. “We hear you on the wait” shows a person read it. Do not explain it away.
  4. Move it offline. Give a phone number or email and offer to listen. Public back-and-forth helps nobody.
  5. Offer nothing in public. A public refund or freebie invites copycat complaints, and you may never offer anything in exchange for a changed or removed review.

Worked examples

These are generated by Review Reply Desk for an invented restaurant, and the test suite recomputes them, so they match what the tool writes today. Always read and edit a reply before you post it.

3 stars: “Nice food but pricey for what you get.”

Hi Jess,

Thank you for taking the time to tell us what worked and what did not. We hear you on how our pricing felt to you, and we will pass it to the people who can act on it. Would you contact us at 555-123-4567? We would like to hear the details and look into it. We appreciate you giving us the chance to do better.

Luigi, Luigi's Trattoria

1 star: “Waited over an hour, the food was cold and the waiter was rude. I want a refund.”

Dear Tom,

Thank you for letting us know, and we are sorry your experience fell short. We hear you on the wait you had, and we will pass it to the people who can act on it. Please reach us at 555-123-4567 so we can look into this properly. We appreciate you giving us the chance to do better.

Luigi, Luigi's Trattoria

1 star, legal threat: “I got food poisoning and my attorney will sue.”

Dear Sam,

Thank you for telling us. We take what you describe seriously and want to understand it fully. Please contact us directly at 555-123-4567 so we can speak with you.

Luigi, Luigi's Trattoria

The special cases

Legal threats, injuries and theft

Do not describe what happened or argue the facts. Two short sentences that take it offline, then tell whoever advises your business before you say more.

Dental, medical and therapy practices

Even when the reviewer shared details, confirming in public that they were a patient can disclose protected health information. Reply in general terms and confirm nothing. This is not legal advice; ask your own adviser about the rules that apply to you.

Reviews that look fake

Check your own records first. If there is no match, report the review to the platform as not based on a real experience and do not accuse the reviewer in public.

Questions

How long should a reply to a Google review be?

Two to four sentences. Long replies are skimmed and long replies to complaints read as defensive. Say thanks, name one specific thing, and for a complaint give a way to reach you.

Should I apologise in a public reply?

Yes, for the experience, not for legal fault. Sorry this was not the experience we want anyone to have admits nothing; we were wrong and it was our fault can. If the review mentions a lawyer, an injury or a theft, keep it to two sentences and take it offline.

Can I delete a bad review?

No. Only the platform can remove a review, and only when it breaks the platform's policies, for example spam, a conflict of interest, or a review that is not about a real experience. You can report it and reply to it.

How soon should I reply?

Within a day or two. A prompt reply tells the reviewer and everyone reading that someone is paying attention.

The model's reply must pass the same checks as the built-in one, otherwise the built-in reply is kept and you are told. The key is kept only in this browser if you tick the box.

4. Ask your customers for reviews

Replies only go so far; more reviews come from asking everyone, the same way. Paste your review link, list your recent customers, and get a text, email or receipt line for each, checked for the things Google and the FTC penalise: offering a reward, asking only happy customers, asking for five stars, or a text with no opt-out. Only message people who gave you their number or email for that.

Your link and customer list are used only to build the messages here; nothing is sent until you tap a send link yourself.

Questions

How do I reply to a negative Google review?

Thank the reviewer, apologise for the experience without arguing or explaining it away, name one specific thing they raised, and move the conversation offline with a phone number or email. Keep it short, use their first name only, and do not offer a refund or ask them to change the review. Paste the review into Review Reply Desk and it writes a reply that follows those rules and checks the result.

Should I reply to every review, including five-star ones?

Yes, if you can keep it up. Replies to positive reviews are short thank-yous that name something specific, and a steady habit of replying is visible to people deciding whether to contact you. Paste a whole batch and the page drafts every reply, with the complaints and anything risky sorted to the top.

Is it legal to reply to a patient or client review?

Not in the way most owners expect. A health practice that confirms in public that a reviewer was a patient can disclose protected health information, even when the reviewer shared details themselves. When you choose Dental, medical or therapy practice, Review Reply Desk writes general-terms replies that confirm nothing, and its checker rejects any reply that refers to the reviewer's visit or care. This is not legal advice; ask your own adviser about your rules.

What do I do about a review that mentions a lawyer, an injury or a theft?

Do not argue and do not describe what happened. Reply with two short sentences that take it offline, investigate privately, and tell whoever advises your business before saying more. The page flags these reviews and writes a short offline reply that says nothing about the claim.

Can I ask the reviewer to change or remove their review?

Not in exchange for a refund, a discount or any other benefit, which platforms prohibit, and asking at all can read as pressure. Resolve the problem privately, then let the reviewer decide. The checker flags any reply that asks for a changed review.

What if the review looks fake?

Look the reviewer up in your own records first. If there is no match, report the review to the platform as not reflecting a real experience, and do not accuse the reviewer in public. The page flags reviews that say things like I have never been there so you can check before you reply.

Does it use AI, and is my data sent anywhere?

Only if you choose to. The reply writer works with no key, using rules and templates in your browser. If you add your own API key for Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, the single review you click Polish on is sent from your browser straight to that provider, never to us, and the model's reply is run through the same checks and replaced by the template if it fails them.

Can I offer a discount or gift for leaving a review?

No. Google's policy prohibits offering incentives for reviews, and the FTC's rule on fake and bought reviews also targets reviews procured for something of value. Do not ask only your happy customers either, which is called review gating and is also against Google's policy. Ask everyone, the same way, for honest feedback. The review request writer on this page checks every message for rewards, gating, requests for a particular rating and missing opt-out lines. This is not legal advice.

Is Review Reply Desk free?

Yes. There is no signup, no review limit and no watermark. It runs in your browser, so it costs nothing to serve. It is MIT-licensed open source you can host yourself.
